prompt: Complete VersionGuardLoader.load so it deserializes a Settings object and returns a status string, telling a serialVersionUID mismatch apart from a missing class, a wrong type and corrupt bytes.
explanation: Every serialized stream records the serialVersionUID of the class that wrote it; when the loading class declares a different value the stream cannot be matched up and ObjectInputStream throws InvalidClassException. Because InvalidClassException extends ObjectStreamException extends IOException, catch blocks must be ordered from most specific to most general or the compiler-legal but useless general catch takes over. ClassNotFoundException is not an IOException at all -- it is thrown when the stream names a type this JVM cannot load.
hints: Wrap the byte array in a ByteArrayInputStream and hand that to an ObjectInputStream; try-with-resources closes it for you.
Order the catch blocks InvalidClassException, then ClassNotFoundException, then IOException -- the reverse order will not compile.
Use instanceof before casting so a stream holding some other type gives "wrong-type" instead of a ClassCastException.
